points.basis:
WHO 2008 places HT5 on the anteromedial forearm, radial to the flexor carpi ulnaris (FCU) tendon, 1 B-cun proximal to the palmar wrist crease. The KMCRIC text matches. I re-measured the right marker at (-0.2452, 0.8569, 0.0368).

LEVEL. Forearm axis from the mean cubital-crease markers (LU5, PC3, HT3: -0.2223, 1.0757, -0.0008) to the mean wrist-crease markers (LU9, PC7, HT7: -0.2614, 0.8312, 0.0436): u = (0.155, 0.972, -0.176), length 0.2516 m, so 1 cun = 0.0210 m (measuring in y only gives 0.0208).
- Projections onto the axis: HT5 s = 0.7884, HT7 s = 0.7662, pisiform proximal extreme (FMA24441 maxY -0.2357, 0.8253, 0.0318) s = 0.7601.
- From the model's HT7, which both reviewers accepted as ok, HT5 is 1.06 cun proximal.
- From the pisiform border, HT5 is 1.35 cun along the axis or 1.52 cun in y only, an excess of 0.35–0.52 cun.
- From the styloid tips (radius minY 0.8296, ulna minY 0.8288), it is about 1.3 cun in y.
- So the excess is 0.05–0.5 cun depending on which crease reference is used.
- HT6 (0.8459) and HT7 (0.835) carry the same systematic offset relative to the pisiform, and both reviewers judged them ok. The HT7–HT6–HT5 spacing on this model is 0.53 / 0.53 cun, which is correct.
- Codex's suggested position (-0.2462, 0.8461, 0.0384) is the HT6 marker's position (-0.2462, 0.8459, 0.0384). Moving HT5 there alone would stack it on HT6 and break the series, so it is not a usable correction.

TRANSVERSE. The two tendon sources disagree.
- muscle.glb (BodyParts3D) slices at y 0.857: FCU FMA38617 x -0.2334 to -0.2278 (z 0.013–0.019), palmaris longus (PL) FMA38463 x -0.2449 to -0.2405, FDS FMA38638 x -0.2481 to -0.2382, FCR FMA38460 x -0.2553 to -0.2494.
- On that mesh the marker is 1.2 cm radial to the FCU edge, about 0.35–0.45 cun more radial than a point just beside the tendon, and near the PL edge.
- The displayed neurovascular layer (vessel-full/nerve-full) disagrees. The superficial branch of the ulnar nerve is at x -0.2478 to -0.2463 (y 0.857) and -0.2442 to -0.2425 (y 0.867). The ulnar artery is at x -0.2516 to -0.2482 (y 0.867) and -0.2464 to -0.2439 (y 0.88).
- So the marker x of -0.2452 lies over the ulnar neurovascular bundle, which is the classic HT5 relation. The two sources are offset by about 1 cm, so the transverse error cannot be measured clearly.
- The marker is radial to FCU in both sources, so it is on the correct side of the tendon.

SKIN. The skin slice at y 0.857 spans x -0.2818 to -0.2206; the anterior surface near x -0.245 is at z ≈ 0.031–0.034, matching marker surface z 0.0338. In the images, the gold dot sits on the ulnar anterior distal forearm, proximal to the carpus, between HT4 and HT6.
points.note: Kept ok (Claude's verdict). The level error is 0.05–0.52 cun depending on the crease reference, which is at or below the tolerance boundary and shared by HT6 and HT7, both accepted. HT5 is 1.06 cun above the accepted HT7. Codex's correction lands exactly on HT6. On the BodyParts3D FCU mesh the marker looks too radial by about 0.4 cun, but the displayed ulnar nerve and artery layer puts it in the right place, so the evidence is mixed. Side issue, not adjudicated here: HT4 (y 0.8629) is only 0.006 m (0.29 cun) above HT5, where 0.5 cun is expected. Any future change to the crease level should move HT4–HT7 together.

points.basis: Level: LI5 y 0.828 to LI11 y 1.0709 is 12 cun, so 1 cun is 0.0202 m and 3 cun is y 0.8887. The marker (surface y 0.8899) is level within about 0.06 cun, so the level is fine. Circumference: I ray-cast the skin contour at y 0.8895. The lateral extreme is x -0.2749 at z 0.003-0.0095. The marker surface point (-0.2737, 0.0124) is about 30 deg anterior of lateral: its offset normal points (-0.0027, +0.0004, +0.0013), i.e. anterolateral. It sits over the anterior edge of the brachioradialis (BR) tendon, which spans skin angle -30 to -7.5, BR surface z 0.0081 to 0.0022. Under the posterolateral face are ECRL at z 0 to -0.0022, ECRB at z -0.004 to -0.006, and APL from z -0.0067 posteriorly. Both neighbours sit behind the lateral extreme. LI5 (-0.2803, 0.828, 0.0081) lies between EPB (-0.2824, 0.0127) and EPL (-0.2720, 0.0073), about 2.0 cm posterior of the wrist extreme (-0.2893, 0.0258). LI7 (-0.270, 0.931, -0.0123) lies over ECRL (-0.2684, -0.0106), about 1.2 cm posterior of its extreme (-0.2717, 0). LI11 (-0.2448, 1.0709, -0.0029) is about 3.5 cm anterior of the elbow extreme (-0.2618, -0.031). Where the LI line should be at y 0.8895: unrolling LI5 to LI11 linearly in arc length gives about 0.6 cm posterior of the extreme, near (-0.274, 0.0). LI5 to LI7 interpolation gives about 1.5 cm posterior, near (-0.270, -0.008). A straight 3D chord gives (-0.2713, 0.0053) inside the skin, which projects to the extreme at z 0.005. Along the skin the marker is 0.7 / 1.27 / 1.7-2.2 cm (0.35 / 0.62 / 0.8-1.1 cun) anterior of these. WHO says 'posterolateral' and both neighbours are posterior of the extreme, so a posterior shift is warranted. Seed check: a lateral ray at (-0.2712, 0.889, -0.005) hits the skin first, exactly at the seed, with normal (-0.87, -0.06, -0.48), i.e. posterolateral; the marker lands at (-0.2742, 0.889, -0.005). The mirrored left seed hits at (0.2717, 0.889, -0.005), 0.5 mm off. The current seed's back ray at x -0.275 misses the skin entirely, so it lies just outside the lateral silhouette.
points.note: WHO location: posterolateral aspect of the forearm, on the line from LI5 to LI11, 3 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease. The KMCRIC text matches. The marker's level is right, but it sits about 0.6-0.8 cun too far anterior around the forearm: on the lateral/anterolateral face in front of the BR tendon, not on the posterolateral face between BR and APL over ECRL/ECRB, where LI5 and LI7 put the line. Move it posteriorly to about z -0.005 on the skin. Codex judged only the y level and the x chord, so it missed the offset around the circumference. Scripts: /Users/nuinuri/workspace/anatomy-worktrees/acupoint-key-filter/.cache/adjudicate/li6-section.mjs (contours) and /Users/nuinuri/workspace/anatomy-worktrees/acupoint-key-filter/.cache/adjudicate/li6-project.mjs (projection check). The 'lateral' surface is chosen over 'back' because the back ray meets this face at about 61 deg incidence and hits a different facet on the left side.

points.basis: WHO p.89: posteromedial wrist, in the depression between the base of the 5th metacarpal and the triquetrum, at the red-white flesh border (ulnar edge of the hand). KMCRIC gives the same location. Bone slices: the right 5th MC (FMA24472) base ends at y=0.8109, where its medial x is -0.2362 at y 0.810. The triquetrum (FMA24439) begins at y=0.8126, with medial x -0.2337 at y 0.814. At y 0.812 only the hamate is present, at medial x -0.2369, so the depression is at y≈0.812. The outer skin contour at y 0.812 (rays inward from [-0.255,0.025]) runs from the dorsum at z 0.0038-0.0047 to the palm at z 0.047. The ulnar border is the medial-most skin, x -0.2243…-0.2250 over z 0.025-0.030. The current marker is [-0.247,0.8029,0.0038] with its surface at z 0.0068. That is the dorsal skin over the 4th/5th MC base, 22.5 mm radial, 9 mm distal and 20 mm dorsal of the target: 31.6 mm, about 1.6 cun at 2.0 cm/cun (LU5/HT3 1.075 to HT7 0.835 = 12 cun). My mirror of the build-anchors axis-ray reproduces the current marker exactly. A medial seed [-0.2245,0.812,0.027] hits the ulnar-border skin at [-0.2245,0.812,0.0270], open air, seed distance 0. The marker goes to [-0.2215,0.812,0.027]. The left mirror hits [0.2232,0.812,0.027], also open. The thigh hits on this ray are at x≥-0.1432 and fall outside the nearest-hit choice.
points.note: Both reviewers agree, and their corrections ([-0.2213,0.812,0.028] and [-0.221,0.812,0.030]) are marker positions, 3 mm outside the same skin point. Use surface 'medial' (from the midline outward). 'lateral' would pass through the thumb side first, and 'back' lands on the dorsum. Out of scope, but noticed: SI5 (surface [-0.2431,0.8368,-0.0028]) also sits on the dorsum, about 1.8 cm radial of the ulnar wrist border (x -0.2247 at y 0.837). After this fix the distal SI line will zigzag until SI5 is reviewed.

points.basis: WHO: posteromedial forearm, between the medial border of the ulna and FCU, 5 B-cun proximal to the dorsal wrist crease. KMCRIC matches. Level: crease about 0.835-0.837 (HT7 0.835, SI5 0.8368) plus 5 × 2.0 cm = 0.935-0.937. The SI5-SI8 midpoint (0.8368, 1.080) minus 1 cun gives 0.938, so y=0.937. The current y of 0.944 is only 0.35 cun high. The transverse error is the real problem. At y 0.944 the ulna (FMA23467) spans x -0.2201…-0.2331 and the radius (FMA23464) x -0.2413…-0.2574. The current marker [-0.236,0.944,-0.0468] (surface z -0.0438) is at x -0.236, over the radius-ulna interosseous gap at the posterior apex of the forearm (contour 270° = [-0.235,-0.0439]). That is radial to the ulna, in the TE corridor (TE7 x -0.239, TE8 x -0.244), on the wrong side of the bone. At y 0.938: ECU (BP45/BP47) covers the posterior ulna to maxX -0.2208 (z -0.0213), and the FCU ulnar head (FMA38619) begins at minX -0.2218 (z -0.0177). They meet at the ulna's posteromedial edge, about [-0.2225,-0.018]. The local skin normal there points about 309° (contour 310° [-0.2152,-0.0336] to 330° [-0.2065,-0.0265]). Projecting the edge along that normal gives skin at about [-0.2115,-0.031]. Inward rays from skin [-0.212,0.937,-0.031] confirm it: along 129° they reach the ECU edge at [-0.2210,-0.0201], then the ulna at [-0.2228,-0.0179]; straight anterior they reach FCU at [-0.212,-0.021]. This is the ulna-FCU interval. New surface vs old: dx 24 mm, dy 7 mm, dz 13 mm, 28 mm total, about 1.4 cun. A back seed [-0.212,0.937,-0.031] hits the skin at [-0.2120,0.937,-0.0309], open air, seed distance 0.1 mm. The marker goes to [-0.212,0.937,-0.0339]. The left mirror hits [0.212,0.937,-0.0318], open. The ray meets no trunk skin.
points.note: Both reviewers call it wrong for the same reason: radial/posterior of the ulna instead of in the ulna-FCU groove. My target is close to Claude's: skin [-0.214,-0.032], at y 0.935. Codex's skin point [-0.220,0.9381,-0.037] is about 8 mm more posterolateral, and inward rays from there pass through ECU to the ulna, so it is over ECU rather than the interval. Use surface 'back': the local normal is more posterior than medial (0.78 vs 0.63). Out of scope, but noticed: SI8 (x -0.222 at y 1.08) is lateral to the olecranon tip (ulna minZ point x -0.2088 at y 1.0602), so SI8 may also need review.

points.basis: WHO p.26: level with the 1st ICS, lateral to the infraclavicular fossa, 6 B-cun from the anterior midline, 1 B-cun below LU2. Transverse scale: ST17 x=-0.090 is 4 cun, so 0.0225 m/cun and 6 cun is x=-0.135. The right coracoid tip (scapula FMA13395 most anterior vertices) is at x -0.126 to -0.138, y 1.347, so it also points to about -0.135. The marker at x=-0.147 is 6.53 cun, 12 mm (0.53 cun) too lateral. Level: bone sections give the 1st ICS at the sternal margin as x=-0.03 between cartilage 2 (FMA7886) top 1.3162 and cartilage 1 (FMA7875) bottom 1.3356, centre 1.326. At x=-0.04 it lies between 1.3174 and 1.3378, centre 1.328. LU2 marker y 1.350 minus 1 cun (0.02445 m from sternal body minY 1.2006 to CV8 1.005 = 8 cun) gives 1.3256. The marker y 1.315 is at the top of cartilage 2, about 12 mm (0.49 cun) low. The combined error is about 17 mm (0.7 cun). In muscle.glb at y 1.327 the clavicular pectoralis major (FMA34690) spans x -0.1535 to -0.098 and the deltoid starts at -0.1497, so the new seed stays on the pectoralis, medial to the deltopectoral boundary. Front ray at (-0.135, 1.327) hits the outer skin at z 0.0412 (0.8 mm from the seed; left mirror z 0.0403), so the marker lands at about z 0.044.
points.note: Both reviewers proposed almost the same fix ([-0.135,1.33,0.04] and [-0.135,1.328,0.043]), and my measurements confirm it. Out of scope but worth flagging: ST14 (1.3149), KI26 (1.3155) and CV20 (1.3164) use the same low 1st-ICS level. Moving only LU1 leaves that row uneven. Also, at y 1.35 the LU2 marker (x -0.150) sits over the clavicular deltoid (medial edge -0.1118), which suggests LU2 is too lateral as well.

points.basis: WHO: on the radial aspect of the forearm, between the APL and EPB tendons, in the APL tendon groove, 1.5 B-cun above the palmar wrist crease. The forearm is supinated (FCR is palmar at +z). Muscle.glb sections at y=0.860: APL (FMA38516) x[-0.2732,-0.268] z[-0.001,0.004]; EPB (FMA38519) x[-0.2668,-0.2573] z[-0.0049,0.0011]; brachioradialis (FMA38486) x[-0.2766,-0.2712] z[0.0073,0.0151]. At y=0.862 the values are similar (APL centre -0.2697,0.0005; BR -0.2731,0.0107). Outer skin contour at y=0.862 (rays toward the limb centre): lateral-most point (-0.2804, 0.012), skin over APL about (-0.273, -0.001). The current front seed hits the skin at (-0.274, 0.862, 0.0257), which reproduces the marker. That is the anterolateral corner of the forearm, palmar to the BR tendon. It is about 31 mm along the skin contour (about 1.5 cun at 0.0206 m/cun) from the APL/EPB interval and on the same palmar-radial line as LU8 (marker x -0.2784, z 0.031). So it is on the wrong side of the named tendons. Level is fine: 1.5 cun above the wrist crease is y 0.8585 (from LU9 0.8276) or 0.862 (from PC7 0.831), so I use y 0.860. A lateral ray at (y 0.860, z -0.001) first hits the outer skin at x -0.2727 (0.3 mm from the seed). The mirrored left seed hits at x 0.2714, so the marker lands at about x -0.2757, over the dorsal-ulnar edge of APL next to EPB.
points.note: Codex said 'unclear' only because it had no tendon coordinates. The model's tendon meshes answer that, and they support Claude's finding. My seed is about 2 mm more dorsal than Claude's [-0.276,0.859,0.001], so it sits on the APL–EPB interval instead of on top of APL. With the lateral projection the marker sits on the radial border just behind the frontal silhouette, so it is best seen from the side.

points.basis: WHO p.30: on the anterolateral wrist, between the radial styloid and the scaphoid, in the depression ulnar to the APL tendon (on the palmar wrist crease). Level: radius minY (styloid tip) is (-0.2773, 0.8296) and the scaphoid spans y 0.820–0.8357, so the marker y 0.8276 is 2 mm distal to the styloid tip at the styloid–scaphoid interval. PC7 at y 0.831 marks the same crease. Side of the tendon: in muscle.glb at y 0.8276, APL is at x[-0.2848,-0.2811] z[0.0172,0.0206] and FCR at x[-0.2633,-0.258] z[0.0327,0.0363]. The marker's skin point (-0.2772, 0.0431) is 4–7 mm ulnar to APL and 17 mm radial to FCR, where the radial artery lies. On the skin contour (lateral-most point (-0.2893, 0.028), palmar maximum z 0.0437) it is on the anterolateral palmar face. Images: the dot is at the radial end of the wrist crease beside the radial artery and over the styloid–scaphoid junction.
points.note: Codex said 'unclear' only because tendon coordinates were missing. The APL and FCR sections place the marker on the correct ulnar side of APL, well within 0.5 cun. No change.

points.basis: I re-measured skin.glb by casting rays from +z to -z, on a grid with 1 mm y steps and 2 mm x steps. The umbilicus is a midline pit 6-9 mm deep. It is deepest at (x -0.0005, y 0.990, z 0.1065), while the flanking skin sits at z 0.114-0.117. The pit rim runs from y 0.980 to 0.995, and its centre is y 0.988-0.990. At CV8/ST25 height (y 1.005) the midline skin is smooth (z 0.1129), with no navel there. The skin close-up agrees. Enlarged 3x, the navel pit sits about 25 px (1.7 cm at 14.8 px/cm, scaled from the 10 cm gap between the dots) below the two gold ST25 dots, about 65% of the way down to ST26 (y 0.979). That gives 1.005 - 0.65*0.026 = 0.988. So the marker is 1.6 cm above the centre of the umbilicus. Cun on this body: the xiphisternal junction (sternal body minY 1.2006) to the navel (0.989) is 0.2116 m / 8 = 2.65 cm per cun. The model's own CV8-CV9 spacing is 2.49 cm. The 1.6 cm offset is therefore 0.6-0.64 cun upward. The lower-abdomen scale, from the bony symphysis top (hip bone FMA16586 near-midline maxY 0.8266) to the navel, is 0.162/5 = 3.24 cm per cun, which gives 0.49 cun. The lateral distance is acceptable: ST17 at x -0.09 marks 4 cun, so 2 cun = 4.5 cm. The marker is at 5.0 cm, 0.22 cun too lateral, so x -0.05 is kept to stay on the straight ST19-ST30 line. Rectus abdominis FMA13377 spans x -0.0088 to -0.0678 at y 0.984-0.994, so x -0.05 stays over the muscle. Seed check with the same rule as build-anchors (front ray): seed (-0.05, 0.989, 0.112) hits the outer skin at z 0.1114 (0.6 mm away), the first front-face hit from outside. The bones cannot decide the level on their own: L3 body front is y 1.0003-1.0306 and L4 body is 0.9652-0.9951, so both 0.989 and 1.005 are plausible umbilicus levels. The skin pit is the direct evidence.
points.note: Codex measured only against CV8 (y 1.005), which the brief calls the umbilicus. But the skin mesh puts the navel centre at about y 0.989, and the skin image shows the dots visibly above the navel. WHO places ST25 2 B-cun lateral to the centre of the umbilicus, so the anatomical navel controls. The error is about 0.6 cun upward, so the verdict is minor and the marker moves to y 0.989 with the same x and z on the skin. The text matches: KMCRIC and WHO both say upper abdomen, 2 cun lateral. Systemic caveat: CV8, KI16, SP15 and GB26 all share y 1.005 and carry the same 1.6 cm error. The 1-cun neighbours are also mis-levelled against the real navel: ST26 and CV7 at 0.979/0.976 are only about 1.0-1.3 cm below it, and ST24 and CV9 at 1.034/1.030 are about 4.5 cm above it. Those should be re-levelled together in a separate pass. Moving ST25 alone does not make them worse, but the ST25-ST26 spacing will look tight (1 cm) until they are fixed.

I took the groove between the tibial border and the soleus front edge, and Claude's lower level. The inflated skin makes the exact skin z interpretation-dependent (about ±5 mm), hence medium confidence. points.basis: WHO: lateral thorax, 6th intercostal space, midaxillary line. Coronal bone sections (x < -0.11), lower edge of rib 6 (FMA8175) to upper edge of rib 7 (FMA8229): at z 0.000 the 6th ICS is y 1.1979-1.2151 (centre 1.2065); at z 0.012 it is 1.1917-1.2078 (centre 1.1998); at z 0.025 it is 1.1848-1.2003.
